To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high-pitch MDCT angiography with low tube voltage (70kV) and Sinogram Affirmed iterative Reconstruction (SAFIRE) can be used to evaluate the aortic morphology in patients with Marfans disease.

1) the use of low-dose MDCT protocols with high pitch values and iterative reconstruction techniques is safe and effective for imaging of aortic aneurysms in Marfan patients; and 2) the reduction of tube current and tube voltage is possible with high-pitch MDCT protocols, which allows a reduction in radiation dose without compromising image quality.

high-pitch dual-source CT angiography (DSCTA) of the thoracic and abdominal aorta in patients suspected of having Marfan disease is feasible at different levels of the effective tube voltage and with Sinogram Affirming Iterative Reconstruction (SAFIRE) and that the radiation dose can be reduced to 1.4 mSv.

the development of an efficient algorithm for the reconstruction of the CT images of the human body from projections.
the development of a new approach to the study of the aorta.
the development of a novel CT-based method for the noninvasive quantification of the aortic wall thickness and the assessment of the aortic dilatation in Marfan patients.

the use of high-pitch MDCT in combination with low tube voltage and iterative reconstruction is a promising approach for CT-angiography of Marfan patients.
CT angiography of the aortic root and ascending aorta is the imaging modality of choice for the initial diagnosis of Marfan syndrome.
